subject: Hosted API: p50/p95 measurement windows & temporary SLO exception workflow
messages:
From: Sophie Miller <sophie.miller@novafin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@novafin.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted API: p50/p95 measurement & short-term exception request

Hi Jonas,

Quick context: we're doing a staged global launch June 7 and expect a handful of high-concurrency bursts in the first 72 hours that will temporarily push our p95 latency above the contracted threshold for the Hosted API. We still need p50 to hold (our product relies on snappy leaderboards) but want to request a short-term exception (72 hours) for p95 while we ramp autoscaling and warming caches.

Can you confirm:
- How Redwood measures p50/p95 for Hosted API (epoch/windowing details)?
- Whether a short-term carveout is possible, and if so what evidence you need to authorize it?

I'm attaching a short request doc with expected traffic patterns and 2-hour charts from our load tests. We'd like to lock something down this week so our legal team can sign an addendum.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Miller
Head of Platform Ops, Novafin

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Miller <sophie.miller@novafin.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@novafin.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API: p50/p95 measurement & short-term exception request

Team — forwarding Novafin's ask. Key points: they want to keep p50 commitments and request a temporary p95 exception for the first 72 hours of their launch window. They attached traffic projections.

Thoughts on a defensible short-term approach: 1) define measurement at 10-minute epochs, compute per-epoch p95, then take the 95th percentile across epochs over a 24-hour window with the ability to carve out explicit planned launch windows (pre-specified start/end). 2) Offer either a 72-hour carveout or a rolling daypart carveout (e.g., 8am–10pm local launch peak) — whichever legal prefers.

What evidence do we need from ops/legal to sign an addendum? Marissa/Ben, can you outline the minimum monitoring artifacts and the drafting timeline for a short addendum? Karthik — are there operational limits we should call out (e.g., sustained concurrency above X requires dedicated capacity)?

-- Jonas

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API: p50/p95 measurement & short-term exception request

Jonas — copying a short proposal. In my view we should:

1) Measurement approach (recommended) — 10-minute epochs. For each epoch compute per-request latencies and derive that epoch's p95. For any agreement window (e.g., 24h, launch-day), compute the overall p95 as the 95th percentile of epoch p95s. This reduces sensitivity to single anomalous bursts while preserving a p95-level signal.

2) Exception duration — offer a single 72-hour carveout tied to Novafin's named launch (explicit start/end). We can also offer an alternative 7-day observation window with documented mitigation steps if legal wants more runway.

3) Evidence/demo package — need observed traffic traces (sampled), load-test artifacts (they supplied), and access to their region/system counts for the launch window. We'll also provide a monitoring dashboard snapshot and a feature-flagged fallback plan (auto-failover to lower-cost model or temporary routing to dedicated nodes).

Attaching a short playbook you can send to the customer (language, required fields for addendum, signature block).

Karthik
[Attachment: proposed-measurement-playbook.md (text)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Miller <sophie.miller@novafin.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@novafin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: p50/p95 measurement & short-term exception request — proposed addendum

Hi Sophie and Contracts team — thanks for the details and the traffic doc. Per internal review, Redwood can support a narrow, auditable carveout for p95 during your launch. Summary of the proposed approach below; if this matches your needs we'll prepare a short addendum for signature and schedule a quick handoff call.

Summary (proposed temporary SLO addendum):
- Duration: 72 hours (explicit start and end datetimes to be provided by Novafin)
- Measurement: compute 10-minute epoch p95s; the SLO for p95 during the contract period will be evaluated as the 95th percentile of epoch-level p95 values across the agreed measurement window. p50 measurement remains unchanged (direct per-request p50).
- Carveouts: planned launch windows (named in the addendum) will be excluded from normal SLO breach remediation; any unplanned region outages or hardware failures will be handled under our standard incident process and do not count as an exception.
- Evidence required from Novafin: load-test artifacts, sample traces for the launch window, and a point-of-contact for real-time escalation.
- Operational mitigations: Redwood will enable prefix caching and prioritize KV warmers for the scheduled window; if sustained concurrency exceeds the dedicated-capacity threshold (TBD — we'll propose numeric thresholds in the addendum) Redwood reserves the right to route traffic to dedicated nodes with mutual notice.

Next steps:
1) Sophie — confirm the exact 72-hour start/end (timezone) and whether you prefer a single contiguous window or up to three non-contiguous windows totaling 72 hours.
2) Contracts — we'll send a 1-page addendum draft (redwood-temporary-slo-addendum.docx) and a HubSpot update (ENG-34567).
3) Ops handoff — Karthik/Ben will prepare the monitoring dashboard snippet and a runbook for warmers.

If you want, we can also offer a short 7-day observation alternative (same measurement, different remediation language) — say the 72-hour carveout +/- a 4-day observation window.

I'll attach the draft addendum and the internal playbook for your review.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
